notes: ToleranceCtx implemented exactly as designed: model_scale is private with no setter and is reachable only through new()/scaled()/model_scale(); new() and scaled() refuse a non-finite or non-positive scale and any non-finite or negative tau with Refusal::UnsupportedEnvelope(EnvelopeCase::ChartDegenerate); scaled() reuses new()'s validation and leaves the taus untouched (BG-TOL-002). The four predicates split cleanly: near_pt and is_small_len are MODEL-SPACE (|a-b| / |l| <= tau_rep * model_scale), sin_margin and is_small_ratio are DIMENSIONLESS (tau_rep alone). entity_tau(boundary_tau) returns tau_rep.max(boundary_tau), reading the entity's own tolerance as its representation error tau_rep; if a later packet intends tau_in or tau_col there it is a one-line change. Certificates on the constructors are Method::Float (H-6: float validation, never Exact). No fifth predicate was added - a scale-aware ratio check or a scaled sin_margin is exactly the category error this type exists to prevent. Tests use a deterministic LCG (fixed seed) and banded random distances so no comparison sits on the float boundary; test-only extraction from Outcome uses unreachable! (not in the H-1 ban list). All four verification commands pass; no legacy item in tolerance.rs was touched.
